name: 30716-loramoe-gptoss20b-1gpu
model: openai/gpt-oss-20b, the mxfp4 release and not a bf16 upcast, served with ONE LoRA adapter: `jeeejeee/gpt-oss-20b-lora-adapter-text2sql` (public, ungated, r=8, lora_alpha=32, targeting q/k/v_proj and `mlp.experts.gate_up_proj` / `mlp.experts.down_proj`). The adapter is part of the setup, not a detail.
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3, one GPU of an a3 node, driver 570.195.03.
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1, `fully_sharded_loras` off. Single-GPU is part of the declaration; do not shard it.
architecture: GptOssForCausalLM sparse MoE, 24 layers, hidden 2880, 32 local experts with 4 active per token, 64 query heads over 8 KV heads, head_dim 64, alternating sliding-window (128) and full attention, mxfp4 expert weights.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=4, warmup the first 10%, cooldown 10%, bounded at 300 requests with an 1800 s safety cap.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, no prefix reuse: 1600 prompt tokens in and exactly 400 out, both pinned min=max, `ignore_eos: true`, `temperature: 0.0`, `request_format: plain` so the wire prompt carries no chat template and is exactly the declared 1600 tokens, seed 30716. Independent random token ids per request.
purpose: A text-to-SQL assistant on a 20-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with a LoRA adapter, serving four concurrent long-prompt requests on one GPU.
launch:
# Launch config: every key goes straight into AsyncEngineArgs.

model: openai/gpt-oss-20b
tensor-parallel-size: 1
enable-lora: true
max-loras: 1

# Taken from the same published `vllm serve` line for this model that supplies max-num-seqs,
# PIECEWISE and prefix-caching below, which declares 32 against a local adapter. This value is
# not cosmetic and is not a property of the adapter file: it sets the shapes and buffer sizes
# the LoRA kernels run at. The loaded adapter is r=8, so ranks 9..32 carry zeros, and the
# kernel shapes match the published serve line's.
max-lora-rank: 32

enable-prefix-caching: false
max-num-seqs: 16

# Pinned, not defaulted: an in-process engine falls through to 2048, a quarter of the budget and
# small enough that a single 1600-token prefill nearly fills a step by itself.
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192

max-model-len: 4096
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90

# Must stay on ONE line as inline JSON; an indented YAML block never reaches AsyncEngineArgs.
# This engine defaults to FULL_AND_PIECEWISE, which for this checkpoint served with an adapter
# is a known-bad combination at this engine version: it emits garbage ("!!!") and runs on past
# the answer, so it is overridden here. `NONE` rather than `PIECEWISE`: inductor compilation is
# unchanged, only graph capture and replay are off, so every decode step issues its own kernel
# launches instead of replaying a frozen node graph.
compilation-config: {"cudagraph_mode": "NONE"}

# dtype/quantization, enforce-eager, kv-cache-dtype, block-size, seed and the remaining LoRA
# knobs are deliberately unset: the checkpoint's own declarations and the engine's own defaults
# are the operating point.
